tasks.short: Monitor plant indications and inspect actual equipment

steps.what: Read computer terminals, gauges, alarms and meters to check equipment condition and trends
inputs: existing plant indications and alarm history

steps.what: Monitor and inspect equipment, switches, valves, safety devices and actual site conditions to detect leaks or malfunctions and assess efficient and safe operation
outputs: operator's observed condition and malfunction assessment

tasks.design: Configure the existing plant-monitoring view in {OPS_SYSTEM} to bring relevant indications and alarm history together. The engineer checks the data and inspects the actual equipment; no alarm suppression, interlock or control action changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant indications can require navigation across screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native monitoring views can reduce screen navigation.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible indication may conceal a sensor fault or physical leak.
tasks.human_edge: Combine field observation with plant indications and recognize uncertainty.

ambition.what: No reduction in physical inspection or increased control span.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: plant monitoring views can consolidate existing indications without replacing physical inspection or control responsibility.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is plant monitoring and historian software. Boundary is monitoring and inspection, not control changes, work-order submission or a separate round report.
Existing instrumentation supplies tag, value, unit, time and status; operator verifies suspect readings in s1-s2. Missing or unreliable indications require field verification, not inferred values.
Native views first. Shares are provisional and count human reading only; existing sensor and alarm runtime earns no saving. Gross 3 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5 net.
unknowns: Current screen navigation burden and instrumentation reliability
research_questions: Can a native view reduce navigation while keeping stale, bad-quality and contradictory indications visible?

already_counted.description: Check displayed indications and source quality

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if screens already suffice; up to 1.5% for smaller navigation gains than central 2.5% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop controlled operating and maintenance procedures

steps.what: Read the actual equipment manuals, existing procedures and change request
Draft operation, safety and maintenance procedure changes from actual source requirements

loop.purpose: Propose procedure wording from selected equipment sources
loop.input: Actual source pages and engineer's requested changes
loop.output: Draft with source-linked steps and explicit unknowns
loop.check: Engineer checks sequence, prerequisites, tags, limits, warnings and omissions against sources and plant context
loop.stop: One redraft then manual authoring; unsupported steps remain unresolved
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates supply structure but varied equipment instructions require reading and phrasing meaning

steps.what: Walk through the draft against actual equipment and obtain operating and maintenance feedback
outputs: verified practical constraints and required corrections

steps.what: Complete and check the procedure revision after the walkthrough corrections
inputs: verified practical constraints and required corrections

steps.what: Independently review and authorize the complete final procedure revision through existing change control
Commit the authorized revision to the controlled procedure library

tasks.design: Use native source indexing and controlled templates in {DOCS} before a bounded wording draft. The engineer verifies the draft against actual equipment, completes corrections and obtains the procedure owner's approval of the final version before committing it; software does not change live plant controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source navigation and first-draft wording take effort alongside technical validation.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked drafting can assist wording within the existing change-control process.
tasks.still_hard: A correct-looking instruction may omit a plant-specific prerequisite.
tasks.human_edge: Verify practical sequence and limits with actual plant knowledge.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-9; controlled document access and operations consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-grounded drafting can assist procedure wording, with independent change-control review required by the modeled plant process.

assumptions: Boundary covers procedure development through controlled version commit. Walkthrough is review, not execution of an unapproved operating instruction.

Equipment owner supplies actual manuals, tags and existing procedure versions; engineer supplies selected changes. Missing or conflicting prerequisites stop drafting pending human resolution. No source pages are fabricated.
Native document functions first. Shares are provisional; owner review is existing other-role work and remains retained. Focal B=90, saving=13.5 share points, gross=15%; 1.5 upkeep gives 13.5% net.
Same-library commit is 1% fully retained. Approval follows the complete final revision and any subsequent edit voids it.
unknowns: Actual change-control authority and source-document quality
research_questions: Can a source-linked draft reduce authoring effort without missed prerequisites or unapproved procedure changes?

already_counted.description: Check source retrieval and proposed wording

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and review recurring source-link errors

approvals.approved_version: authorized final procedure revision from s5; edits void owner approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero when all wording requires manual authoring; up to 9% with more correction than central 13.5% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Contact equipment specialists to resolve a problem

steps.what: Retrieve the actual equipment identity, manual references and observed fault information
inputs: actual observed problem and available diagnostic records

steps.what: Prepare and finish checking the equipment-support request and selected manufacturer or specialist contact
outputs: checked complete support request and recipient

steps.what: Send the checked support request to the manufacturer or appropriate specialist
inputs: checked complete support request and recipient

steps.what: Discuss the actual equipment problem with the manufacturer or specialist and clarify the advice and its limits
outputs: clarified troubleshooting advice and unresolved questions

tasks.design: Use native equipment-reference links in {OPS_SYSTEM} and a support-request template in {EMAIL}. The engineer supplies actual fault details, finishes checking the request before sending it and personally discusses the specialist's response on {TELEPHONY}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment identifiers and repeated support-request headings require navigation and typing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native references and email templates can reduce repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: A specialist cannot diagnose confidently from incomplete or misleading observations.
tasks.human_edge: Describe the actual plant problem and challenge advice that does not fit the installation.

ambition.what: No autonomous troubleshooting or equipment changes.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5; equipment information and external disclosure access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native equipment references and request templates can reduce repeated support-contact preparation without resolving the technical problem.

assumptions: Boundary is contacting and discussing with a specialist, not performing a repair, changing settings or issuing a purchase order. This route uses a written request followed by a technical call.

Equipment owner supplies existing ID and support contact; engineer supplies actual observed faults. Missing diagnostic information is manually clarified within retained discussion, not generated from the equipment model.
Native templates first. Shares are provisional; final request checking stays in ordinary authoring rather than a new approval step. The short send is 1% fully retained.
Gross 5.5 minus 0.5 upkeep leaves 5 net. Changed content or recipient invalidates the finished-request gate.
unknowns: Current support-request preparation effort and disclosure rules
research_questions: Can templates reduce repeated identifiers and headings without obscuring actual fault symptoms?

already_counted.description: Verify retrieved details and finish the support request

incremental.description: Maintain support-request template and contact references

approvals.approved_version: complete checked request and recipient at end of s2; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero for call-only requests or existing effective templates; up to 3% with smaller preparation gains than central 5% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure and record actual fuel use

steps.what: Weigh or measure the actual fuel used and verify the applicable quantity and unit
inputs: actual fuel and weighing or metering equipment
outputs: operator-verified actual fuel quantity and unit

steps.what: Enter and finish checking the actual fuel quantity, unit, equipment reference and measurement period in the fuel-use log
inputs: operator-verified actual fuel quantity and unit

steps.what: Save the checked fuel-use entry in the same fuel log

tasks.design: Configure native equipment and period defaults in the fuel log {OPS_SYSTEM}. The engineer still measures the actual fuel, enters and checks the quantity and saves the completed entry; no new sensor feed or inferred fuel consumption is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated equipment, period and unit entry adds effort after measuring.
tasks.enabler_now: Native log defaults can reduce repeated fields.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong units or period boundaries can distort the record despite a correct reading.
tasks.human_edge: Verify the measurement and what interval it represents.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4; fuel log access and operator consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native log defaults reduce repeated fields without measuring fuel or establishing its actual use.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the fuel-use log. Boundary includes actual weighing or measuring, entry, check and save; billing and fuel procurement are separate.

Engineer produces actual quantity, unit and measurement period in s1; equipment owner supplies existing equipment ID and permitted units. Missing values require remeasurement or explicit uncertainty, not inferred sensor data.

Native defaults first. Shares are provisional and only repeated entry changes; measurement runtime already performed by instruments earns no labour credit. Entry checking stays in ordinary authoring, with no extra self-approval task.
Same-system save is 1% fully retained. Gross 5.1 minus 0.5 upkeep leaves 4.6 net.
unknowns: Current log defaults and actual repeated-field burden
research_questions: Can native defaults reduce typing while preserving correct quantity, units and measurement period?

already_counted.description: Enter and check actual fuel-use data

approvals.approved_version: complete checked fuel-use entry at end of s2; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if defaults already exist; up to 3% with smaller entry gains than central 4.6% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Engineers retain plant inspection, control responsibility and actual measurement; native views, forms and controlled drafting assist documented work.
skills_to_grow: Keep actual readings separate from default metadata
role.ambitious_version: Traceable operating records and controlled procedures without moving plant authority to software.
